item.title: China Books French, Argentine Wheat as Global Prices Slump
item.description: At least two cargoes of French wheat and one from Argentina were booked for China last week, according to people familiar with the matter, signaling that a major buyer is snapping up the grain after a slump in global prices.

item.title: Vanguard Says Tax-Loss Inflows to Muni ETFs Likely to Stick
item.description: Tax-loss harvesting has turbocharged the growth of municipal-bond exchange traded funds in 2026 at the expense of open-end mutual funds, which may lose much of those assets for good, according to Vanguard Group.

item.title: US Treasury Futures Retreat as Markets See More Fed Hikes
item.description: The Treasury market selloff unleashed by hot October inflation data is poised to deepen when bond trading resumes on Thursday, price action in the futures market suggests.

item.title: Chile Trucker Protest Over Fuel Prices Imperils Farm Exports
item.description: A protest by truckers and regional buses over fuel prices and roadway tolls was snarling traffic across Chile on Wednesday, threatening exports of fresh produce at the start of the country’s agricultural season.

item.title: Aging Boomers Are Key Factor Supporting Corporate Bond Market
item.description: Ordinary Americans seeking to lock in relatively high income have been surprisingly heavy buyers of US corporate bonds this year, emerging as an important source of demand for the securities even as yields have soared in recent months.
